title: Affine morphisms and quasi-coherent algebras (relative spectrum)
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A *quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebra* is a sheaf $\mathcal A$ of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_S$-module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. (1) If $f:X\to S$ is an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism], then $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebra. (2) For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebra $\mathcal A$ there are an affine morphism $\pi:X\to S$ (the relative spectrum $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)$) and an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_S$-algebras $\alpha:\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_*\mathcal O_X$ such that for every affine open $U\subseteq S$ the morphism $\pi^{-1}(U)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ corresponding (morphisms into an affine scheme) to the ring map $\alpha_U:\mathcal A(U)\to\Gamma(\pi^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_X)$ is an isomorphism of schemes; in particular $\pi^{-1}(U)$ is affine. (3) The functor $(f:X\to S)\mapsto f_*\mathcal O_X$, on morphisms $(h:X\to X'\text{ over }S)\mapsto(f'_*h^\sharp:f'_*\mathcal O_{X'}\to f_*\mathcal O_X)$, is an anti-equivalence from the category of schemes affine over $S$ (morphisms: $S$-morphisms) to the category of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebras, with quasi-inverse $\mathcal A\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)$ of (2); for an algebra map $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and an affine open $U\subseteq S$, the restriction of the corresponding $S$-morphism $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal B)\to\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)$ over $U$ is, under the identifications of (2), $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_U):\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal B(U)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$. (4) The anti-equivalence is compatible with restriction to an open $V\subseteq S$: $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)\times_SV=\pi^{-1}(V)=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_V(\mathcal A|_V)$ and $(f_*\mathcal O_X)|_V=(f|_{f^{-1}(V)})_*\mathcal O_{f^{-1}(V)}$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (part (1)).* Let $f:X\to S$ be affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so by [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] (Schemes, Lemma 01LC) $f_*\mathcal O_X$, an $\mathcal O_S$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] via $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_S\to f_*\mathcal O_X$, is quasi-coherent. Its sections $(f_*\mathcal O_X)(U)=\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}U)$ are commutative rings, the restrictions are ring maps and $f^\sharp_U$ is a ring map, so $f_*\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras, hence a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebra.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma 01S8 ((2) implies (3), first three sentences)

proof.text: *Step 2 (the local pieces).* Let $\mathcal A$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebra. For an affine open $U\subseteq S$ identify $U=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_S(U)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (the morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_S(U)$ corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal O_S(U)}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], an isomorphism since $U$ is affine) and put $X_U=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ with $f_U:X_U\to U$ induced by the structure map $\mathcal O_S(U)\to\mathcal A(U)$. For affine opens $V\subseteq U$ let $\rho^U_V:X_V\to X_U$ be $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the restriction $\mathcal A(U)\to\mathcal A(V)$; it is a morphism over $U$ because the restriction is compatible with the structure maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-affine-inclusion](ii) $\rho^U_V$ identifies $X_V$, over $V$, with the open subscheme $f_U^{-1}(V)$ (condition (a) of relative glueing), and by its part (iii) $\rho^U_U=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho^U_W=\rho^U_V\circ\rho^V_W$ for affine $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ (condition (b)).

*Step 3 (part (2): the scheme $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)$; it is affine over $S$).* By Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-relative-glueing-affine-opens] there are a morphism $\pi:X\to S$ and isomorphisms $i_U:\pi^{-1}(U)\to X_U=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ over $U$, for every affine open $U\subseteq S$, such that $i_U\circ(\pi^{-1}V\hookrightarrow\pi^{-1}U)\circ i_V^{-1}=\rho^U_V$ for affine $V\subseteq U$. Put $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A):=(X,\pi)$. For every affine open $U$, $\pi^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ is affine, so $\pi$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism].

*Step 4 (part (2): the isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal A\to\pi_*\mathcal O_X$).* For an affine open $U\subseteq S$ let $\alpha_U:\mathcal A(U)\to\Gamma(\pi^{-1}U,\mathcal O_X)=(\pi_*\mathcal O_X)(U)$ be the composite of the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal A(U)\cong\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U),\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with the map on global sections of the isomorphism $i_U$; $\alpha_U$ is a ring isomorphism, and an $\mathcal O_S(U)$-algebra map because $i_U$ is a morphism over $U$. For affine $V\subseteq U$, taking global sections in $i_U\circ(\text{incl})\circ i_V^{-1}=\rho^U_V=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal A(U)\to\mathcal A(V))$ shows $\alpha_V(a|_V)=\alpha_U(a)|_{\pi^{-1}V}$. The affine opens form a basis of $S$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis](a) (sheaves of commutative rings) the $\alpha_U$ are the components on affine opens of a unique morphism of sheaves of rings $\alpha:\mathcal A\to\pi_*\mathcal O_X$, an isomorphism by its part (b); the two morphisms $\mathcal O_S\to\pi_*\mathcal O_X$, $\alpha\circ(\text{structure map})$ and $\pi^\sharp$, agree on affine opens, hence are equal by part (a), i.e. $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_S$-algebras. Finally the morphism $\pi^{-1}(U)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ which corresponds to $\alpha_U$ under [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] is $i_U$ (both have the ring map $\alpha_U$ on global sections, and that bijection is injective), an isomorphism of schemes; this proves (2).

source.place: Constructions, proof of Lemma 01LV (first paragraph: the isomorphisms A(U) → R(U) on affines, compatible with restriction, glue by Sheaves 009U) and Lemma 01LX (3)

proof.text: *Step 5 (the functor).* For an $S$-morphism $h:X\to X'$ between schemes $f:X\to S$, $f':X'\to S$ affine over $S$, and an open $U\subseteq S$, $h^{-1}(f'^{-1}U)=f^{-1}U$, so $h^\sharp$ gives ring maps $(f'_*h^\sharp)_U:\mathcal O_{X'}(f'^{-1}U)\to\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}U)$, compatible with restrictions, and compatible with the structure maps from $\mathcal O_S(U)$ because $f'\circ h=f$; by Step 1 this is a morphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebras $f'_*\mathcal O_{X'}\to f_*\mathcal O_X$. $(\mathrm{id})^\sharp=\mathrm{id}$ and $(h'\circ h)^\sharp=h_*(h^\sharp)\circ h'^\sharp$ make $f\mapsto f_*\mathcal O_X$ a contravariant functor.

*Step 6 (part (3): the functor is fully faithful).* Let $f:X\to S$, $g:Y\to S$ be affine over $S$; for an affine open $U\subseteq S$ put $X_U=f^{-1}U$, $Y_U=g^{-1}U$, both affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. (i) By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] ($Y_U$ affine, $Y_U\cong\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(Y_U)$) $k\mapsto k^\sharp$ is a bijection from morphisms $X_U\to Y_U$ to ring maps $\Gamma(Y_U)\to\Gamma(X_U)$; and $k$ is over $U$ iff $g\circ k=f$ on $X_U$, iff (both being morphisms into the affine $U$, same lemma) $k^\sharp\circ g^\sharp_U=f^\sharp_U$, i.e. iff $k^\sharp$ is an $\mathcal O_S(U)$-algebra map. (ii) Faithful: if $S$-morphisms $h,h':X\to Y$ have $g_*h^\sharp=g_*h'^\sharp$, then for every affine $U$ the restrictions $X_U\to Y_U$ have the same ring map, hence are equal by (i); the $X_U$ cover $X$, so $h=h'$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. (iii) Full: let $\varphi:g_*\mathcal O_Y\to f_*\mathcal O_X$ be an $\mathcal O_S$-algebra map. For affine $U$ let $k_U:X_U\to Y_U$ be the $U$-morphism with $k_U^\sharp=\varphi_U$ (by (i)). For affine $V\subseteq U$, $k_U|_{X_V}$ and $k_V$ (followed by $Y_V\subseteq Y_U$) are morphisms $X_V\to Y_U$ into an affine scheme with ring maps $\mathrm{res}\circ\varphi_U$ and $\varphi_V\circ\mathrm{res}$, equal by naturality of $\varphi$; so they are equal. For affine $U,U'$, $X_U\cap X_{U'}=f^{-1}(U\cap U')$ is covered by the $X_V$ with $V\subseteq U\cap U'$ affine, on each of which $k_U$ and $k_{U'}$ both equal $k_V$; so $k_U$ and $k_{U'}$ agree on $X_U\cap X_{U'}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] (uniqueness), and the same lemma glues the $k_U$ to $h:X\to Y$ with $h|_{X_U}=k_U$. Then $g\circ h=f$ (they agree on every $X_U$), and $g_*h^\sharp$ and $\varphi$ agree on every affine $U$ (both are $\varphi_U$), hence are equal by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis](a).

proof.text: *Step 7 (part (3): essential surjectivity, the quasi-inverse and $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_U)$).* By Steps 3–4 every quasi-coherent $\mathcal A$ is isomorphic to $\pi_*\mathcal O_X$ for the affine $\pi:\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)\to S$; with Step 6 the functor is an anti-equivalence and $\mathcal A\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)$, with $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ sent to the unique $S$-morphism $\Phi:\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal B)\to\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)$ with $\pi_{\mathcal A*}\Phi^\sharp=\alpha_{\mathcal B}\circ\varphi\circ\alpha_{\mathcal A}^{-1}$, is a quasi-inverse (in particular every $X$ affine over $S$ is $S$-isomorphic to $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(f_*\mathcal O_X)$, Morphisms 01S8 'moreover'). For an affine open $U$ the restriction $\Phi_U$ of $\Phi$ over $U$ has the ring map $\alpha_{\mathcal B,U}\varphi_U\alpha_{\mathcal A,U}^{-1}$, so $i_{\mathcal A,U}\circ\Phi_U\circ i_{\mathcal B,U}^{-1}:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal B(U)\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U)$ has the ring map $\varphi_U$ on global sections (Step 4: the ring map of $i_U$ is $\alpha_U$), as has $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_U)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] they are equal.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01SA (proof) and Lemma 01S8 ('Moreover'); Constructions, Lemma 01LY (restriction over affines)

proof.text: *Step 8 (part (4): restriction to an open $V\subseteq S$).* $(f_*\mathcal O_X)|_V=(f|_{f^{-1}V})_*\mathcal O_{f^{-1}V}$, since both have sections $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}W)$ on opens $W\subseteq V$, with the same restrictions and structure maps. $\mathcal A|_V$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-algebra: a point $s\in V$ has an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $\mathcal A|_U=\widetilde M$ [pqf-def-coherent], and a basic open $s\in D(r)\subseteq U\cap V$; by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] the sections of $\widetilde M$ on the basic opens $D(rr')$ of $D(r)=\operatorname{Spec}R_r$ are $M_{rr'}$, compatibly with restrictions, as are those of $\widetilde{M_r}$ on $\operatorname{Spec}R_r$, so $\mathcal A|_{D(r)}\cong\widetilde{M_r}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] $\pi^{-1}(V)$ with $\pi|:\pi^{-1}(V)\to V$ is $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A)\times_SV$. The affine opens of $V$ are the affine opens of $S$ contained in $V$; so $\pi|$ is affine, and with the same $i_U$ ($U\subseteq V$ affine) and $\alpha|_V:\mathcal A|_V\cong(\pi|)_*\mathcal O_{\pi^{-1}V}$ it has all the properties of (2) for $\mathcal A|_V$, i.e. it is $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_V(\mathcal A|_V)$ (unique up to unique $V$-isomorphism by (3) over $V$). Restricting an $S$-morphism of schemes affine over $S$ to the preimages of $V$ corresponds to restricting the algebra map to $V$, by the first sentence; so the anti-equivalences over $S$ and $V$ commute with restriction.
